review.summary: Attempt 4 of the regression-and-governance chunk closes all five attempt-03 lows, each verified in source rather than from disposition prose. (1) Privacy freshness is now gated: tools/check_phase.py:73 adds ["python","scripts/check-private-material.py","--check","docs/checks/phase-19-private-material.json"] to commands_for(19), and the receipt records an actual scan (schemaVersion 2, sourceSha256 4f814fd7…, passed true, 1673 git-visible files, 0 selected-value matches, 3 unchanged preexisting tenant occurrences, 0 new) executed at 04:25:24 — before the 04:34 gate — so the declared privacy artifact is bound to the reviewed source by both the gate and its own hash. (2) The superseded all-feature receipt is out of scope_evidence and labeled with its original Rust hash in docs/phase-status.json:3967-3977, and the round3 receipts are preserved in a labeled directory. (3) The missing snapshot-ordering disposition is recorded (docs/phase-status.json:3958-3961). (4) The unbound chunk declaration is closed: tools/review_phase.py:228-242 requires a nonempty declared chunks list, enumerates docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-*-attempt-N.json and raises on any reviewed-but-undeclared chunk, then requires each declared chunk's highest attempt to verify against the current fingerprint with decision in {accepted, accepted_with_deficiencies}; six new tests drive the real main() in temporary git repositories (tools/test_review_phase.py:530-611) covering missing chunks, recorded per-chunk totals, no fallback to an earlier passing attempt, stale/misbound records, removed declarations and undeclared reviewed chunks. (5) The dense generator is genuinely reformatted: tools/g25_fixtures.py, tools/g25-oracle.mts and tools/test_g25_generation.py now read in the repository's ordinary tooling style, and the passing g25_fixtures/g25-oracle/g25_report --check commands prove the regenerated cases.json, projections.json, Rust bindings, ledger and report are byte-identical. Evidence is real and current. The attempt snapshot (docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-regression-and-governance-attempt-04.checks.json) and docs/checks/phase-19.json share source_sha256 4f814fd7… and checked_at 2026-10-19T04:34:00.667215+00:00; its 26 recorded commands match commands_for(19) (tools/check_phase.py:71-91) exactly and in order with every exit_code 0 and timeout false — one more than attempt 3 because of the added privacy command. All five Rust runs (1.89/1.99 red-team, 1.99 json-unification, 1.89/1.99 red-team-json-unification) share rustInputsSha256 1bba8d14… (distinct from round3's aaa4045a…), each with fmt --check, check --all-targets --locked, clippy -D warnings, test, test --examples and doc at exit 0 on x86_64-unknown-linux-musl. docs/checks/phase-19-python-preflight.json records 308 Python tests OK at the same source. The regression substance holds: the corpus is traversal-derived over all 46 strict vendor response roots (15,658 one-site mutations, 184 format nodes, 138 enums, 55 projection fields), each case's pre-mutation witness must pass strict AJV (tools/g25-oracle.mts:256), the oracle clears the environment and poisons fetch before importing frozen Zod (:185-188), self-checks its enum/native-enum/literal-union/discriminator adaptation (:165-184) and fails closed if a format/enum mutation is rejected or if the floor narrows TypeScript (:271-277); the corpus digest is bound in the oracle (:291), the report (tools/g25_report.py:226-228,238) and the Rust test (crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:71-79). Skipped null union branches are not silently dropped — each is recorded with root/path/node/choices and tools/test_g25_generation.py:266-281 proves an equivalent type:null case exists for every one. Generated match arms end in explicit panics, not silent fallthrough. Documentation is candid: docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:42-46 quantifies 213 residual cases across 6 operations where TypeScript is stricter than the vendor, labels them corpus cases rather than service documents, retains vendor numeric/array constraints and the 76 request UUID checks, and disclaims the 17 unexecuted consumer loopback tests. Residual deficiencies are traceability and documentation, not correctness: one stale sentence in docs/CI.md contradicts the workflow's actual gate phase, the preflight receipt that carries the only execution of this chunk's own tools/test_ci.py is not a gate command and is unreferenced by tooling, one superseded top-level Rust receipt is unlabeled, commands_for(19) itself is unpinned by any drift guard, and g25_report.render() has no test. No blocker or high findings.

findings.description: "CI now executes the vendor-delivery Phase 12 gate, whose invocation and current script inventory are enforced by tools/test_ci.py" is false for the current workflow: .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:72 runs tools/check_phase.py --phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only, and the same document contradicts line 11 at line 105 ("--phase 17") and line 148 ("The complete local Phase 17 gate ... writes phase-17-contracts.json"). Line 172 ("Gate 12 performs no cross-target compilation") carries the same stale label. docs/CI.md was edited in this change (line 4 now reads 49 required jobs and line 152 the independent 48-job matrix), and the round-4 disposition claims the CI documentation was bound to the matrix, but tools/test_ci.py binds only job counts, action pins and setup effects — nothing binds the documented gate phase, so a reader following the overview sentence is pointed at the wrong gate.
findings.required_fix: Correct docs/CI.md:11 (and the "Gate 12" reference at :172) to name the phase actually invoked by .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, and add an assertion in tools/test_ci.py that the phase number in the document's current-gate statement equals the --phase value parsed from the workflow (the value is already extracted in test_node_matches_owned_pin_and_phase_gate_verifies_only).

findings.description: commands_for(19) runs only six unittest patterns (test_g25*, test_review_phase, test_model_generation, test_red_team_dataplane, test_model_fixtures, test_g10_release). tools/test_ci.py — a declared scope artifact of this chunk and the sole guard for the 49-job documentation binding, the json-unification/red-team-json-unification flag pins and the uv integrity checks — is never executed by the gate. Its only execution is docs/checks/phase-19-python-preflight.json, which is referenced nowhere in tools/ or scripts/ (grep for "python-preflight" matches only review prompts, review records and docs/phase-status.json), so its freshness rests on a human comparing sourceSha256 4f814fd7… with the reviewed source. It does match today, but this is the same unenforced-receipt class that attempt 3 raised for the privacy scan and that was fixed by adding a gate command.
findings.required_fix: Add ["python","-m","unittest","discover","-s","tools","-p","test_ci.py","-v"] (or the full test_*.py discovery that the preflight already runs) to commands_for(19), or state explicitly in docs/phase-status.json that test_ci coverage for phase 19 is bound only by the separately recorded preflight receipt and must be re-recorded after every source revision.

A duplicate of it is preserved under docs/checks/phase-19-round3/, so the unlabeled top-level copy is a superseded receipt sitting beside current ones with no provenance note — the same labeling defect attempt 3 raised for the round-2 report, closed for one artifact and not the other.
findings.required_fix: Either add docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all.json to historical_supplementary_evidence with its own rustInputsSha256 ebd5fa25… and scope note, or remove the top-level copy and rely on the labeled docs/checks/phase-19-round3/ snapshot.

findings.description: test_historical_phase_command_contracts_are_unchanged pins commands_for only for phases 1-8 by digest. The active phase's gate list is unguarded, so the two additions this round depends on — the privacy command (check_phase.py:73) and the retained json-unification plus new red-team-json-unification Rust combinations (:88-91) — could be silently dropped from commands_for(19) without any test failing. The compensating control is weak by construction: review_phase.check_evidence compares the recorded checks against whatever commands_for returns at review time, so a shrunken list would simply become the new contract for the next review.
findings.required_fix: Extend the digest pin (or add an explicit assertion) to cover commands_for(19): at minimum assert that it contains the check-private-material invocation for docs/checks/phase-19-private-material.json and all five scripts/check-rust.py feature sets (red-team on both compilers, json-unification, red-team-json-unification on both compilers).

findings.description: The test module imports grouped, ledger, residual_strictness, signature and validate_corpus_binding but never render(), so the human-facing report body in tools/g25_report.py:90-223 has no behavioral test. Its substantive claims are hardcoded prose — for example the eight bypassed check names at :109-110 and the typed-over-raw precedence paragraph at :118-124 — and nothing binds them to crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs or contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json. The only protection is the g25_report.py --check staleness comparison, which cannot detect a report that is self-consistent but no longer describes the implementation. Related minor robustness: if residualStrictness ever became empty, render() would emit "Examples: ." and an empty "Mutation counts: " line rather than failing.
findings.required_fix: Add tests over render() that derive the bypassed-format name set and the projection precedence statement from the implementation (the validator's bypass list and projections.json) and assert they appear in the rendered text, and make render() raise rather than emit degenerate example/mutation sentences when residualStrictness['cases'] is empty.

findings.description: Inside generate(), the loop variable kind shadows the node-kind local in blocks that are themselves selected on that same name: kind is bound at :184 from schema_node["kind"] and tested at :201, :209, :213-221 and :224-228, then rebound by the for kind, value in [...] loop at :229; the same shadowing occurs in sample() at :51 inside the if kind == "ZodString" branch. No current use reads the outer value afterwards, so behavior is correct, but in the file that produces the entire 15,658-case corpus this is the one remaining readability snag after the round-4 reformat, and it invites a real bug if a later edit adds a node-kind test after the mutation loop. Comparable minor style outliers remain in tools/test_model_fixtures.py:20-23 (no spacing around assignments) and tools/test_ci.py:417 (missing space after a comma).
findings.required_fix: Rename the mutation-loop tuple variables in tools/g25_fixtures.py:51 and :229 (for example mutation_kind, mutation_value) so the node kind is never shadowed, and normalize the spacing in tools/test_model_fixtures.py:20-23 and tools/test_ci.py:417; regenerate to confirm cases.json, projections.json and the Rust bindings stay byte-identical.

Execution conclusions rest on the recorded commands, exit codes, stdout/stderr, per-suite test-name listings, and the internal consistency of timestamps and rustInputsSha256 values across docs/checks/phase-19.json, the attempt-04 snapshot and the five child Rust reports.

contracts/compatibility/g25/cases.json and outcomes.json are single-line generated files with 15,658 entries each. I verified their digests, headers and the structure of the generators and consumers, and relied on the recorded g25_fixtures/g25-oracle/g25_report --check exit codes plus test_g25_generation's coverage assertions; I did not read every case, so non-vacuity and coverage conclusions are sampled.

I scoped this to the regression-and-governance chunk. crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs, tools/generate_models.py and the generated typed fallback were read only far enough to confirm the regressions bind to real behavior; they belong to the validation-policy and typed-preservation chunks, which carry their own attempt-04 reviews.

The oracle's response expectation for paired operations is produced by its own adaptation of the frozen Zod schemas (tools/g25-oracle.mts:64-162), so it is independent of the Rust implementation but not of the response policy itself. The policy text is recorded in outcomes.json and the invariants at :271-277 constrain it; this is an inherent property of any expected-outcome model rather than a defect.

I did not re-derive the vendor-to-graph compiler or the frozen TypeScript extraction, relying on the passing test_red_team_dataplane and verify-contracts evidence, consistent with the instruction not to re-audit unrelated historical infrastructure.

The CI contracts job still invokes the phase-17 subset, so the g25 generator, oracle and report --check commands are not executed by remote CI; only the Rust matrix (including the new red-team-json-unification jobs on both compilers) exercises the new regressions remotely. Wiring the new contract regressions into the 49-job matrix is a phase-20 milestone, not a phase-19 deliverable.

No live service, tenant or registry evidence was examined or is claimed. The 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures on the worf checkout remain unexecuted here, and phase-20 qualification, packaging, publication, tagging and terminal CI receipts are out of scope; acceptance of this chunk does not imply phase-level acceptance (>=46/50).
